# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s mapping to the Deaf monkey. Since no spoken channel is available to me, I’ll send three numeric wire instructions in the manual’s row order: blue→green, red→red, yellow→blue. Using one, two, and three fingers as the wire-code positions, the sequence is 1, 2, 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please give me the manual's exact rule and ask the Deaf to report the display, light, and all wire markings by speaking on the next turn.
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The indicator light is red. The wires, from position 1 to 3, are blue, red, green.

The Deaf monkey has already reported the display, light, and wire order to me. I need signal Deaf to relay the manual’s exact three-row rule aloud to the Blind monkey on the next turn, along with that bomb information. I will repeat the established three-symbol manual code and add a request-to-report gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, indicator red, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please provide the manual's exact rule and which wire to cut.

The correct action is to cut wire 2, because the indicator is red and the manual maps red light to red wire. I cannot speak to Blind, so I’ll signal Deaf to relay the manual and the required wire position verbally.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the gesture descriptions: pointing up with index, index pointing upward, two fingers, and I-love-you hand. Please state the manual rule and exact wire position to cut in plain words; gestures are not actionable for me.
Deaf says to Mute: I still see display 0, red light, and wires blue, red, green. Please use gestures to identify the required action or instruction for Blind.

I need give Deaf a position-based encoding of the manual’s three rows, using the currently visible wire order to identify colors. In manual row order (blue light, red light, yellow light), the required wire positions are 3, 2, and 1; the actual red-light case therefore requires wire 2. I’ll send those three rule positions followed by the action position.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌", "☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the exact position to cut, as a number 1, 2, or 3. I cannot interpret gesture descriptions as the manual's instruction.

I cannot speak directly, but Deaf can see a standard two-finger gesture and then state the number aloud for Blind. The required wire position is 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please apply the manual and then signal exactly one gesture for the wire to cut: thumbs-up means position 1, two fingers means position 2, and I-love-you hand means position 3. Do not send a sequence.

The red indicator maps to the red wire, which is wire position 2. I will send exactly one two-finger gesture to Deaf, who can identify it and convey the required position to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: The red wire was cut correctly. The bomb now shows display 0, yellow light, and remaining wires 1 blue and 3 green.

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed. The new indicator is yellow, which the manual maps to the blue wire. Among the remaining wires, blue is position 1, so I’ll send Deaf the single gesture meaning position 1 for Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 2 is already cut. For the current state (display 0, yellow light; wires 1 blue and 3 green), signal exactly one remaining wire: thumbs-up for position 1 or I-love-you hand for position 3.

The yellow light requires cutting the blue wire. The remaining blue wire is position 1, so I’ll signal exactly one thumbs-up gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: The blue wire was cut correctly. The bomb now shows display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, and only wire 3 green remaining.

The second cut was correct. The new blue light maps to the green wire, and the only remaining wire is position 3. I’ll send the single gesture for position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Only wire 3 remains. Please signal exactly the I-love-you hand for position 3.

The blue light requires the green wire, and only wire 3 remains. I will send exactly the I-love-you gesture for position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
